title: Timestamp
description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp with nanosecond precision. All persisted timestamps are UTC; offsets are normalized at the transport edge and never stored (docs/03).
x-invariants: The trailing 'Z' is mandatory. A stored timestamp with a non-zero offset is invalid, not merely non-canonical.
Nanosecond precision is the storage contract; consumers MUST tolerate a shorter fraction, producers SHOULD emit nine digits.
Clock drift is a first-class signal (docs/08, WI-163). A source whose clock is outside the accepted skew window marks the feed unhealthy rather than being silently trusted.
